title: Pauri 25, sound: bahutaa karam
tomorrow: Pauri 25, meaning: even hunger is a gift

lines: A GRANDMOTHER WHO COOKS FOR ALL.
cards: A grandmother cooks for everyone who walks through her door. Plates keep coming out of the kitchen, and nobody gets a bill. Ask her how much she's made, and she laughs.
She's never counted. Keeping score isn't how she thinks. Pauri 25 starts with a giver like that.

teach.b: The first line, in the original: bahutaa karam likhiaa naa jaae. Bahutaa: so much, so great; you heard it yesterday in bahutaa aakheeai bahutaa hoe. Karam is a word to be careful with.

It looks like karma, but Sikh commentators read karam here as a different word, from Persian and Arabic, meaning generosity, kindness, grace. Not what you've done, but what's given to you. Likhiaa: written.
Naa jaae: cannot be. So: His generosity is so great it cannot be written down. That's the same honesty as the last few stanzas, the writing runs out, but now about giving.

teach.h: NOT A SESAME SEED OF GREED.
teach.b: The next line, in paraphrase: the great Giver doesn't have even a sesame seed of greed. That's til again, the sesame seed from Pauri 21. The Giver wants nothing back, not even that much.
Listen to the rhythm. Bahutaa karam: two strong beats, a lift. Likhiaa naa jaae: falling softly, like setting something down.
Sikh practice has its own picture of a giver who doesn't count.

The langar, the gurdwara's free kitchen, feeds anyone who comes, of any faith or none, sitting together on the floor, and nobody tallies who ate. Tomorrow the stanza goes somewhere surprising: to hunger and pain.

how: Pauri 25 is recited in the morning Japji Sahib; the giving it describes is echoed in the langar, the free community kitchen of the gurdwara, where anyone is fed.

o: a heavy debt that must be paid back
a ritual duty set by scripture

games.q: the sound of Pauri 25 — tap the pairs.
p: not a sesame seed of greed

s: karam in Pauri 25 means the same as karma
Sikh commentators read it as generosity or grace, from Persian and Arabic.
Pauri 25 says the Giver has not a sesame seed of greed
it feeds anyone who comes, of any faith or none.

games.q: you ask the great Giver of Pauri 25 what's wanted in return. what's the answer?
games.why: vaddaa daataa til na tamaae: the great Giver hasn't a sesame seed of greed. the giving can't even be written down.

practice: Say the line aloud, bahutaa karam, likhiaa naa jaae, once slowly, feeling the lift and the fall, then twice more, softer.
Then bring to mind three things you were given this week that you didn't earn: a smile, a meal, a kind word, a sunrise. Don't count them up; just let them arrive.
